page: Amazon Web Services c8id.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyper-threading) running at 3.9 GHz, backed by a 480 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2202.0 and high single-threaded throughput in gzip compression (34.39 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.52 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show relative weaknesses. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and PassMark memory score fall into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Large-block memory bandwidth is average, with read speeds of 41.59 GB/sec and write speeds of 31.72 GB/sec.

The c8id.xlarge is designed for workloads requiring high single-threaded compute power and fast local NVMe storage, such as text processing, web serving, and lightweight database operations. Its low memory-to-vCPU ratio (2 GB per core) and weak multi-core scaling make it less suitable for memory-intensive applications or heavy multi-threaded tasks like large-scale LLM text generation, where it achieves only 4.81 tokens/sec on medium models. Qualitatively, it offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound tasks that benefit from dedicated Intel Xeon execution and high-speed local storage without requiring massive memory footprints.
